mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates on future cash flows reduce the present value of expected equity returns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in all months with FEDFUNDS increases >0.25%, or the effect of FEDFUNDS on returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for two consecutive months predicts increased labor market flexibility, lowering risk premia and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when UNRATE is below 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by at least 10% month-over-month is accompanied by rising corporate hiring, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following large PAYEMS jumps, forward returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO reading above 105 suggests robust industrial production, reducing supply-side bottlenecks and increasing expected corporate profits, which results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day periods with INDPRO >105, 20-day forward returns are negative on average or fail to outperform a baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in a month, it indicates weakening consumer demand, which elevates uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >5% in the current month
failure_condition: In months with large HOUST declines, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% each month signal dual headwinds in economic activity, raising risk and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↓2% AND RSAFS ↓2% in the same month
failure_condition: In months with the specified dual decline, 20-day forward returns are not negative or are statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.00%), the 20-day forward return for the S&P 500 tends to be higher than in a tightening regime, regardless of other signals, due to lower borrowing costs and increased investment.
failure_condition: In the easing regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than in the tightening regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for three consecutive months, it reflects stronger labor market conditions and lower wage growth expectations, which reduce equity risk premia and produce positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the three-month UNRATE decline, 20-day forward returns are not positive or are not statistically significant (p > 0.1).
